וילקח — the bridegroom 'will be TAKEN' (לקח): Elijah's removal-verb (2 Kgs 2:9-10) and Isa 53:8's ('he was taken — לקח — from prison and from judgment'). The removal of the bridegroom is told in the Servant's own verb.

verses.translation: Then{H227} he said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: The standing grain{H7054} is plentiful{H7235}, and the reapers{H7114} are few{H4592}.

one_way_hebrew: קמה (H7054) — the standing grain of Deut 16:9, ripe for the sickle (מהחל חרמש בקמה), the word already met at 6:30. Greek θερισμός ('harvest') names a season; the Hebrew shows the uncut field waiting — Joel 4:13's 'put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (9:37): מעטים] מועטים A.

verses.translation: Entreat{H2470} now{H4994} the face{H6440} of the owner{H1167} of the standing grain{H7054}, that he send{H7971} many{H7227} reapers{H7114} to reap{H7114} his grain{H7054}.

one_way_hebrew: חלו נא פני — Mal 1:9's exact syntax: ועתה חלו נא פני אל ('and now, entreat the face of El') — the same חלה-פנים intercession idiom the Gadarenes misused at 8:34, here commanded rightly: entreat the Owner's face for reapers. Greek δεήθητε ('pray ye') keeps the request and loses Malachi.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 9 in the Shem Tov Hebrew narrates its healings in Scripture's own clauses and carries several readings no Greek text has. (1) 9:2 grounds the pardon: 'Yeshua saw their faith... By the FAITH OF EL (באמונת האל) your iniquities are forgiven' — Deut 32:4's אל אמונה made the basis of forgiveness; Greek has only 'thy sins be forgiven.' (2) 9:30 reuses Gen 3:7 whole — ותפקחנה עיני שניהם ('the eyes of them both were opened') — enacting Isa 35:5; the mute of vv. 32-33 continues Isa 35:6, the signs in Isaiah's order. (3) 9:24 = Gen 19:14 verbatim (ויהי כמצחק בעיניהם); 9:36 = Num 27:17 verbatim (כצאן אשר אין להם רועה); 9:13 = Hos 6:6 in Hosea's consonants, introduced by the rabbinic 'go and learn' and closing 'I came not to TURN BACK (להשיב) the righteous but the wicked' — the teshuvah Luke 5:32 must add in Greek is already in the Hebrew verb. (4) 9:20: the woman grasps the TZITZIT (Num 15:38) — healing sought where Mal 3:20's 'healing in its kanaph' hangs; 9:38 commands 'entreat the face (חלו נא פני, Mal 1:9) of the owner of the standing grain (קמה, Deut 16:9).' (5) 9:34: the charge is 'by the NAME of the demons' (Greek: 'by the prince'); 9:22 carries the scribal reverence-formula בש״ית ('by the Name, blessed be He'); 9:9 names the evangelist מתתיה (Mattityah), glossed 'Matyeo' — the Hebrew-to-foreign gloss on the book's own author. (6) 9:10-11: 'many VIOLENT (פריצים, Dan 11:14) and wicked men' dine — no tax collectors; the objectors are 'the sages' (9:3) and the title is 'your rav' (9:11). (7) 9:28-29 lack the Greek's 'Do you believe?' dialogue and the eye-touching — straight to 'your faith will heal you.' (8) The whole raising-section 9:18-26 is absent from the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew; Shem Tov carries it in full, with the captain asking in Deut 32:39's own verb — והחיה, 'make her alive.' (9) 9:15: the bridegroom's companions cannot 'WEEP AND FAST' (Zech 7:3-5's fast-day pair; Greek only 'mourn'), and the bridegroom 'will be TAKEN' (לקח, Isa 53:8). (10) 9:35 'cities and TOWERS' with Vat. Ebr. 100 against Greek 'villages'; healing 'every disease (מדוה)' reverses Deut 7:15's curse. Scan corrections to the transcription: 9:2 אמונתם (not מחשבותם), 9:6 אז + מיטתך, 9:9 עבר + מאט״יאו, 9:12 אינם, 9:14 קרבו, 9:16 מהמלבוש, 9:18 אדו׳, 9:20 שופעת, 9:23 רבים, 9:25 ויגע בידה, 9:35 בשורות, 9:36 כצאן + אין. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 9 (Perek 38), 14 (39), 18 (40), 27 (41), and 32 (42).
